episodes.190722: A front moved through the area as isolated severe storms developed along the front producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.190835: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms tracked across the South Plains on the evening of the tenth. Storms formed within the vicinity of a remnant mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) from convection from the previous day. A couple of thunderstorms became severe producing both severe wind gusts near Morton (Cochran County) and large hail up to 2.25 inches in diameter in Brownfield (Terry County).
episodes.190850: Thunderstorms produced gale-force wind gusts over portions of the lower tidal Potomac River and middle portion of the Chesapeake Bay during the late evening hours.
episodes.192073: Gusty storms along the coast produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.192544: Deep tropical moisture associated with a tropical disturbance centered just offshore Tampa Bay produces 5-8 inches of rain with locally higher amounts leading to flooding across parts of Sarasota County. An isolated multi-day total of 12.87 inches reported near Siesta Key along coastal Sarasota County represented the maximum observed total associated with the event.
episodes.192601: Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall from the 10th into the morning of the 11th led to urban and river flooding across portions of western-north Texas. The most significant flooding occurred across Knox and Baylor Counties.
episodes.192852: A frontal boundary was stalled along the Gulf Coast from Texas to Florida. As afternoon peak heating was reached, scattered thunderstorms began to develop along the coast of Louisiana in the vicinity of the stalled front. One storm produced a waterspout.
episodes.192907: A surface front was stalled across north Florida with moist, unstable southwest flow off of the Gulf of Mexico south of the front. This airmass combined with frontal lift and sea breeze forcing triggered locally heavy rainfall and isolated strong to severe storms across portions of NE FL.
episodes.192998: A plume of deep tropical moisture streamed into South Florida during the week of June 10 through 15th as the region remained south of a stationary boundary and in close proximity to a weak tropical disturbance. Multiple mesoscale convective systems developed to the south of this boundary over Central Florida and gradually pivoted southward into South Florida during the morning and afternoon hours of June 11th, 12th, and 13th, 2024. With a very moist and warm atmospheric composition, rainfall rates were efficient and tropical in nature.
episodes.193000: A plume of deep tropical moisture streamed into South Florida during the week of June 10 through 15th as the region remained south of a stationary boundary and in close proximity to a weak tropical disturbance. Multiple mesoscale convective systems developed to the south of this boundary over Central Florida and gradually pivoted southward into South Florida during the morning and afternoon hours of June 11th, 12th, and 13th, 2024. With a very moist and warm atmospheric composition, rainfall rates were efficient and tropical in nature. Storm total rainfall of up to 20 inches occurred across NE Miami-Dade and SE Broward counties, with totals as high as 18 inches in the Big Cypress National Preserve in Collier County. These rainfall totals resulted in major flooding across these areas.
episodes.193074: A pulse-severe thunderstorm formed rapidly over south central Hidalgo County and soon after dropped a microburst that tore the roof from a poorly constructed building, as wellas peeled back a section of garage door, in Mission.
episodes.193598: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a surface trough produced gusty winds across portions of the Maryland coastal waters.
episodes.193600: A few thunderstorms produced damaging winds in Runnels and Sutton counties and localized flash flooding in Taylor County.
episodes.193636: A weak, convectively enhanced upper-low over the Texas/New Mexico border aided in the development of severe thunderstorms ahead of this feature. This included hail, damaging winds, and a couple of brief tornadoes.
episodes.193638: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across west Texas during the early morning. This mesoscale complex caused wind damage across portions of the northeast Permian Basin.
episodes.193713: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Black River at Black Rock for a short time on June 11, 2024.
episodes.193736: A two-day period of active, regenerative convection occurred from early June 11th through late in the evening of the 12th, 2024, as a low level ridge axis remained to the east.  Strong upper-level divergence remained over the Florida Keys along with a deep tropical airmass and little if any convective inhibition.

Multiple observers reported a brief cone tornado to the northeast of Loop. The tornado only lasted two to three minutes over open fields. The tornado likely dissipated near US Highway 83. No damage was reported and this tornado is rated EF-Unknown. Path is estimated from reports and radar data.

Other minor damage occurred at Mission Fire Station 4, where the bottom of a garage was peeled back.

Significant flash flooding from an initial round of excessive rainfall occurred in NE Miami-Dade County. Social media and broadcast media footage depicted stretches of roadways with stalled-out cars extending from northern sections of Miami Beach across to Miami Shores, North Miami, and Aventura. A total of 5 to 7 inches of rain fell in this area during this event. ||This was the first round of flash flooding associated with the event, with a second round of excessive rainfall occurring on June 12th in the same areas. A complete listing of impacts will be included in the June 12th Flash Flood event entry for Miami-Dade County.

A flash flood warning was issued for southeastern Broward County on the afternoon of June 11th after portions of Hallandale Beach and Hollywood received four to six inches of rain in six hours. The large amount of rainfall across the urban region resulted in significant flash flooding. Social media and broadcast media footage depicted stretches of roadways with stalled-out cars. ||This was the first round of flash flooding associated with the event, with a second round of excessive rainfall occurring on June 12th in the same areas. A complete listing of impacts will be included in the June 12th Flash Flood event entry for Broward County.
